profile.reading:
This is Facebook/Meta Altoona Data Center 4 on Meta's Altoona, Iowa campus. Meta broke ground on the Altoona campus in 2013 and has expanded it seven times since, most recently announced in December 2024, per Meta's own fact sheet and Data Center Frontier's reporting; Meta has invested more than $2.5 billion in the city of Altoona and the state of Iowa through this campus. Construction has employed an average of about 1,000 workers a year over twelve years, totaling 8.7 million work-hours, with peak skilled-trade staffing of 1,300 workers; day-to-day operations employ more than 400 people. Meta reports operational buildings on the campus are LEED Gold certified, that it matches all of its global electricity use with 100% clean and renewable energy, and that a Meta-supported project added 225 megawatts of new renewable generation capacity in Iowa. Meta says it has made more than 300 grants and sponsorships in the area since 2015 and provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Polk County-area schools and nonprofits. Meta does not publish a specific street address, building count, or per-building square footage for individual Altoona structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

Iowa has drawn more than $17 billion in data center capital investment, with 27 data centers operating or under construction statewide as of 2025, according to Inside Climate News; Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Apple together account for nearly all of that total. The state has led the nation in wind generation since adopting the first state renewable portfolio standard in 1983, with wind now supplying about 60% of Iowa's electricity and helping keep industrial power prices among the eighth-lowest in the country, both factors regional reporting ties directly to hyperscale operators' site selection in the Altoona/Des Moines corridor. That same reporting states Meta's Altoona campus has used up to 16% of the city of Altoona's water supply and consumed roughly 1.2 million megawatt-hours of electricity annually, and flags that federal cuts to clean-energy tax incentives under the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act are projected by Energy Innovation to raise Iowa industrial electricity rates by 14 to 26 percent, a risk regional press has connected to the pace of further hyperscale investment in the state.

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity, square footage, or a building count for the Altoona campus; regional press (Data Center Frontier, citing Meta's own December 2024 announcement) reports the campus as a whole will exceed 5 million square feet on completion, expected in 2025, making it Meta's largest data center campus worldwide, surpassing Prineville, Oregon's 4.6 million square feet. No per-building figure is asserted here.

profile.regional_context: Altoona sits in the Des Moines metro area of central Iowa. Meta chose the site in part for MidAmerican Energy's wind-heavy generation mix and Iowa's wind-energy tax credits; MidAmerican has said it supplies its Iowa customers, Meta included, with wind generation matching 100% of retail load on an annual basis. Iowa's data center cluster in the Altoona/Des Moines area also includes Microsoft, Google, and Apple facilities, and the sector has become a significant driver of the state's industrial electricity demand and a subject of debate over local property-tax abatement policy, according to Inside Climate News and the Bend Bulletin-style local reporting seen in other Meta markets.

reading.body:
Meta's Altoona campus in Polk County is a major hyperscale data center investment, with $2.5 billion committed since groundbreaking in 2013 and 400-plus operational jobs once fully built. The specific power capacity is not published by Meta, so this campus cannot be ranked by megawatt draw against other facilities. Iowa has only 2 facilities with published power figures in its current mapped inventory of 52, for a state total of 18 megawatts of disclosed capacity, meaning most data center power in the state remains unreported and Altoona's actual demand is unknown.

The campus operates under LEED Gold certification for operational buildings, qualifying it for energy-efficient hosting of large-scale compute workloads. Meta has matched the campus electricity use with 100 percent renewable energy procurement as part of its net-zero operations, and is funding 225 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity in Iowa to support its facilities in the state. This investment in behind-the-meter and grid-scale renewables suggests the operator views the site as part of its long-term scaling infrastructure.

Without a published megawatt figure from Meta, the campus cannot be assessed against grid constraints or ranked within the state's data center power hierarchy, despite the substantial capital deployed and the operator's clear intent to make Altoona a major footprint. The absence of capacity disclosure is the binding limit on reading this site's role in AI scaling.
